11.titre: U1·Seq2 — Reading: an e-mail from Finland (résumé original, p.21)
lignes: An e-mail from Kirsi, a sixteen-year-old Finnish girl.
She introduces herself and asks about Amel's country.
On weekdays she gets up early and goes to school by bus.
She has classes in the morning and in the afternoon.
She rarely goes out at the weekend.
Her family has a dog and a parrot.
She lives in a small village called Tikkakoski, in Central Finland.
Finland is famous for its saunas and lakes.

12.titre: U2·Seq1 — Listening: Sindbad the sailor (résumé original, p.48-49)
lignes: Sindbad the sailor tells the story of his first voyage.
He inherited money from his father but spent it quickly.
He became a merchant sailor to make money.
He sailed from Baghdad to Basra, then through the Gulf to the Far East.
The sailors stopped at an island that was really a whale.
A king's horseman helped him and took him to a cave.

13.titre: U2·Seq2 — Reading: Okonkwo & Unoka (résumé original, p.53)
lignes: Okonkwo was well-known in the nine villages.
He was tall and huge, and he looked fierce.
At eighteen, he beat Amalinze the Cat in a wrestling match.
He was a hard worker and became a wealthy farmer.
His father Unoka was thin, lazy and improvident.
Unoka loved music and did not like war.
Okonkwo was very different from his father.

14.titre: U2·Seq3 — Reading: Alice in Wonderland (résumé original, p.59)
lignes: It was spring, and Alice was sitting in the garden.
She had nothing to do and felt sleepy.
Suddenly a white rabbit passed near her.
The rabbit took a watch out of its pocket.
Alice followed it down a hole and kept falling.
She saw a little bottle marked 'DRINK ME'.

15.titre: U2·Seq3 — Reading: Coketown (Hard Times, résumé original, p.57)
lignes: Coketown was a town of red brick and black smoke.
It was full of machinery and tall chimneys.
The river ran purple with ill-smelling dye.
The people all looked the same and worked in factories.
There was neither a leisure centre nor a library for children.

16.titre: U2·Seq4 — Fables: The Stork & The Oak Tree (résumés originaux, p.68)
lignes: A thirsty stork found a pitcher with only a little water.
It could not reach the water with its beak.
It dropped small stones into the pitcher one by one.
The water rose, and the stork drank.
A giant oak tree was uprooted by a storm.
It asked the small reeds how they survived.
The reeds said they bent with the wind.
The oak stood stiffly, and so it broke.

17.titre: U3·Seq2 — Reading: a survey on computer use (résumé original, p.83)
lignes: A report about computer use by 60 young people.
All the teenagers had a computer at home.
They all used the computer to play games.
28 did some word-processing at home.
16 kept addresses and phone numbers on it.
Only 6 used it to learn programming.
